questions.question: When being passed, where should a motorcyclist ride in the lane?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed from behind or by an oncoming vehicle. Riding closer to the passing driver creates danger for both of you.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, where should you ride in the lane?
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may make the driver try to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: At an intersection, making eye contact with an oncoming driver:

options.text: Means the driver definitely sees you.
Does not guarantee the driver sees you.
Is required before you can proceed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee the driver sees you.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver sees your motorcycle. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but still fail to notice them.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have more time to react to other drivers.

questions.explanation: Space between vehicles gives you time to react and room to maneuver safely. Limited escape options is a disadvantage, not a benefit.

questions.question: Which is NOT a common helmet type?
questions.explanation: The two main helmet types are three-quarter and full-face. Full-face helmets offer the best protection.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually maintain control if the motorcycle stays upright and straight.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:
questions.explanation: At night, increase your following distance. Slow down and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign appears on the back of slow-moving vehicles traveling below 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: When other vehicles are stopped or slowed, you should:

options.text: Weave in and out of traffic lanes.

questions.explanation: Weaving between stopped or slow vehicles is dangerous. Vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to ride safely.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles on your right with no oncoming traffic, ride:

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked vehicles on your right with no oncoming traffic. This helps you avoid car doors opening and pedestrians stepping out. If oncoming traffic is present, stay in the center of your lane for maximum space.

questions.question: You should keep a greater distance between your motorcycle and other vehicles:

options.text: If you can see through the vehicles in front of you to check traffic conditions.

questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. When the pavement is slippery, when you cannot see past the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy, keep at least a four-second distance between you and the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: A helmet will protect you best if it has all of the following qualities, except:
questions.explanation: A helmet works best when it meets U.S. DOT safety standards, fits snugly around your head, and has no damage like cracks, loose padding, or torn straps.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes occur at speeds below 30 mph and during short trips of less than five miles.

questions.question: A difference between goggles and a windshield is:

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
A windshield protects your eyes from wind, but goggles do not.
A windshield prevents your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, a rider should:

options.text: Use their arms to steer, not to hold themselves up.
Sit far back enough that their arms are straight when reaching the handlebars.
Keep their knees away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use their arms to steer, not to hold themselves up.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can easily reach all controls. Keep your arms slightly bent and use them to steer. Press your knees against the gas tank to help you balance during turns.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You will have time to react to dangers.
You will have room to move.
You will have more time to speed up when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to speed up when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you react faster and gives you room to move if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection carefully.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same thing as a red traffic light. You must stop and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Sit so your arms are straight when reaching the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your elbows should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars. Press your knees against the gas tank to help you balance.

questions.question: Eye protection is:

options.text: Required only for new motorcycle riders.

questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all motorcycle riders to wear eye protection while riding. A full face shield provides the best protection for your eyes.

questions.question: It is illegal to operate a motorcycle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: In California, riders age 21 and older cannot operate a motorcycle with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Riders under 21 cannot ride with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. It is unsafe to ride even if your BAC is below the legal limit.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcyclists must pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next one begins.

questions.question: If passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may exceed the speed limit until the pass is complete.
You may disregard no passing zone markings if you began the pass in a passing zone.
You must observe the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must observe the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: Always stay within the posted speed limit when passing. Only pass in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light means the signal will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: When riding at night, maintain a minimum following distance of:
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distances. Keep at least three seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols and tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, it is usually best to:

options.text: Use the shoulder of the road to slow down before crossing the tracks.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Ride straight across angled railroad tracks. Changing your path could push you into another lane and cause a collision.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Slow down, let the dog approach, and accelerate away from the animal.
Park and wait for the dog to lose interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, let the dog approach, and accelerate away from the animal.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, slow down and let it catch up. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols and tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: When riding over scored pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look downward to see the changes in the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: When riding on scored pavement, look ahead, not down. Ride slowly, keep a steady speed, and do not fight the handlebars.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols and tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road ahead is slippery when wet.
